key_insight: Odd elasticity persists in selected isotropic and high-symmetry strain-gradient stiffness tensors, but non-Hermitian wave dynamics requires anisotropy.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports continuum modeling and design of active, nonreciprocal metamaterials with intrinsic length scales and controllable wave amplification or attenuation.
method: Classify fourth-, fifth-, and sixth-order odd stiffness tensors across 3D point-group symmetries.
Derive governing equations, higher-order boundary conditions, and the generalized acoustic tensor using dynamic virtual work.
Numerically analyze wave dispersion in a transversely hemitropic odd elastic continuum.
evidence_signal: Analytical results establish Hermitian acoustic tensors in isotropic and hemitropic limits, while numerical analysis of a transversely hemitropic example reveals exceptional points and simultaneous wave-component amplification and attenuation.
watch_item: The abstract reports theoretical and numerical results, not experimental validation or a demonstrated microstructure-to-continuum homogenization procedure.
paper_title: Odd Elasticity in Strain-Gradient Continua: Anisotropy Classification and Non-Hermitian Elastodynamics
